note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors. Nominations were received on Tuesday 5 May 1936 and there was no contest in any division: the Unionists nominated for the 21 divisions in which they held majorities and the Nationalists for ten, and the retiring members for the divisions without a nomination were deemed re-elected (Mid-Ulster Mail, 9 May 1936, p. 9; Ulster Herald, 9 May 1936, p. 5). Polling in County Tyrone was fixed for Wednesday 3 June 1936; no poll was needed. The new council first met on Monday 8 June 1936 (Ulster Herald, 13 June 1936, p. 5). No nomination was received for Fintona (Ulster Herald, 9 May 1936, p. 5), so the retiring member was deemed re-elected. Division inferred from the 31 May 1933 return (Philip M'Caffrey; Irish News, 19 April 1933, p. 6); he attended the Board of Guardians on Saturday 13 June 1936 (Ulster Herald, 20 June 1936, p. 9, block image read) and spoke at the council meeting of 20 June 1936 (Ulster Herald, 27 June 1936, p. 3). He was again deemed re-elected for Fintona in 1939. No co-option or by-election for the division was found in the 1936 reports read. Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
